rv.q: It is a darkly funny, shocking production – one unlike anything I have seen on the stage in a long time.
Entwined with director Ola Ince's precise, crisp visual language the production, despite its debt to film, becomes transfixingly theatrical.
These irritations are offset by its always crisp, entertaining and outrageous script.
I certainly kept watching, but couldn't help wondering – given how many huge issues are now in play in the real-world – if the whole affair isn't a case of fiddling while Rome burns.
Is God Is is a blazing revolt against victimhood and a marvellous account of how the meek could well inherit the world.
And this remains a stunning, preternaturally timed production.
Visually, the production is stunning and subversive, with Chloe Lamford building upon the playful pacing and direction of Ince.

cn.t: Harris' darkly comic revenge tale thrills with cinematic direction and propulsive energy, though its deeper meaning proves more elusive than its visceral journey.
